Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a short list of contract items we need clarity on before we can move to PO:

1) Output ownership: we need confirmation that EdgeWorks will own rights to outputs generated by our prompts (including downstream commercial use).
2) Training/data use: we cannot allow our data to be used to further train third-party models — we need either an explicit opt-out or carveout in the MSA/Order Form. Please clarify proposed language and any commercial impact.
3) Feedback license: we understand you collect telemetry/feedback to improve models — we need the scope limited to non‑identifying telemetry and a clear non-exclusive license for model improvements.
4) Telemetry retention & auditability: procurement requires retention window and ability to request audit logs for a 3rd party review.

I've attached our RFP excerpt for context (EdgeWorks_RFP.pdf). Can you send your suggested redline and an estimate of any fee delta for training opt-out? Ideally we need a redline by EOD Friday so procurement can route the PO next week.

Thanks,
Marta Gomez

Marta — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing what we can offer and our proposed redlines (sending a draft doc attached: redwood-proposal-v1.docx):

- Output ownership: EdgeWorks will retain ownership of customer-provided prompts and the raw outputs produced for EdgeWorks’ API calls. We propose an explicit clause in the Order Form: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Outputs."

- Training/data use: Redwood will NOT use Customer Prompt or Output data to update or train any models used for third-party customers, unless Customer opts in. We propose two paths:
  a) Default: Customer data is eligible for aggregate telemetry used for service quality improvements but is NOT used for model weight updates.
  b) Opt-in training: Customer can opt-in to allow training on a separate agreement with a fee or credit.

- Feedback license: Redwood requests a limited, perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to Customer Feedback solely for the purpose of improving and operating Redwood services (no right to sublicense for unrelated products).

- Telemetry retention & auditability: Standard telemetry retention is 90 days; we can provide export of audit logs on request within SLA. If EdgeWorks needs a longer retention or a third-party audit export, we can provide on a case-by-case basis (may be subject to additional charges).

Next steps:
- I will loop in Legal (laura_bennett) and Sales Ops (Ben) to draft MSA redlines and quantify the training opt-out delta.
- Can you confirm whether you require attribution language in outputs, or if a simple ownership clause suffices?

Attaching redwood-proposal-v1.docx with proposed Order Form bullets.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Soojin / Ben —

Attached is a tracked redline (msa-redline-edgeworks-track-changes.docx) and below are high-level notes / proposed clause text to include in the MSA + Order Form. I focused on minimizing downstream risk and keeping commercial options flexible.

1) Outputs / Title (Order Form):
Proposed sentence: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to any output (\"Outputs\") generated by the Services in response to Customer input. Provider shall have no right, title or interest in Customer Outputs except for any limited rights expressly granted in this Order Form."
Risk note: this is straightforward; remove any implicit assignment language elsewhere in the MSA (e.g., developer work product).

2) Training & Model Updates (MSA - Data Use):
Proposed clause: "Provider will not use Customer Data (including Prompts and Outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider models used in production for other customers, unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in. Provider may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service stability and security monitoring (not to update model weights)."
Risk note: Good protection. If the customer insists on a complete ban on any telemetry collection, that materially increases operational costs and may reduce our ability to detect abuse; recommend fee to compensate.

3) Feedback License:
Proposed clause: "Customer grants Provider a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free license to Customer Feedback solely to operate and improve the Provider's services. Provider will not sublicense or otherwise transfer Feedback outside its service improvement processes; Feedback will be de-identified where feasible."
Risk note: Keep scope limited and tie to product improvement only. Avoid broad intellectual property assignment language.

4) Telemetry retention & Audit access:
Proposed language: "Provider retains telemetry logs for the period specified in the applicable Order Form (standard: 90 days). Upon Customer request, Provider will export relevant audit logs within the SLA window. Extended retention or third-party audit exports may be provided subject to additional charges and scheduling constraints."

5) Evidence & Compliance:
We should attach our SOC 2 overview and provide a path for the customer to request narrower extracts rather than full data dumps. Prepare a short evidence package to attach to the redline.

Timeline: I can deliver the tracked redline by EOD Thursday (2026-12-03) — attached. I also recommend a 30-minute alignment call with EdgeWorks' legal+procurement.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
